doc.title: Joe Temperley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

chapter: Woody Herman, Buddy Rich and Thad Jones
title: Waiting for the Local 802 card and working at Korvettes
summary: Six-month union wait in 1965, during which he sold audio equipment.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Did you have to wait to get into the union?
Yes. It took six months to get into the union, Local 802. It doesn’t take that, it takes six minutes now, or even six seconds. They’re dying to get people in the union.
Oh, yes. But at that time it was like a six month wait. So I waited it out.
What did you do during those six months?

I worked in Korvettes, selling audio equipment. And that was an experience too of course. All of a sudden you know I went from playing every night, playing my saxophone and all that, all of a sudden I’m working in a retail store. But it served its purpose.
That’s right. It puts things in perspective for you.
